title: 尉迟杯·隋堤路
title_en: To the Tune Yu Chi Bei: The Road Along the Sui Dyke
author: 周邦彦

readings.zh: 这里是“一层层”的意思，读 chóng。
readings.en: Here it means layer upon layer, so it is read chóng.

readings.zh: 这里是“常常”的意思，读 cháng，不读 zhǎng。
readings.en: Here it means "often", so it is read cháng, not zhǎng.

readings.zh: 这里指栏杆，读 jiàn，不读 kǎn。
readings.en: Here it means a railing, so it is read jiàn, not kǎn.

readings.zh: 这里同“娼”，指歌女，读 chāng，不读 chàng。
readings.en: Here it means a singing girl, so it is read chāng, not chàng.

readings.zh: 这里是“仍然、又”的意思，读 hái。一说是“回来”的意思，读 huán。
readings.en: Here it means "still, again", so it is read hái. Another view takes it as "to return", read huán.

glosses.zh: 隋堤：隋炀帝开挖运河（汴河）时，在河边筑的长堤，堤上种满了柳树。宋朝时汴河从京城开封流过。
glosses.en: suí dī: the Sui Dyke, a long bank built along the canal (the Bian River) dug by Emperor Yang of Sui, planted all along with willows. In the Song, the Bian River flowed through the capital, Kaifeng.

glosses.zh: 密霭：浓浓的雾气。
glosses.en: mì ǎi: thick mist.

glosses.zh: 阴阴：昏暗的样子。
glosses.en: yīn yīn: dim and dark.

glosses.zh: 笼沙：月光淡淡地笼罩着沙岸。
glosses.en: lóng shā: pale moonlight wraps the sandy bank.

glosses.zh: 还宿：又要住宿在。
glosses.en: hái sù: again to stay the night at.

glosses.zh: 画舸：画着彩色花纹的船。舸，大船。
glosses.en: huà gě: a painted boat. Gě means a large boat.

glosses.zh: 烟波：水面上像烟一样的雾气。
glosses.en: yān bō: mist lying over the water like smoke.

glosses.zh: 南浦：南边的水边。古人常在“南浦”送别，后来就用它指送别的地方。
glosses.en: nán pǔ: the southern shore. In old poems people often said goodbye at the southern shore, so it came to mean any place of parting.

glosses.zh: 行人：出远门的人，这里是诗人自己。
glosses.en: xíng rén: a traveller, here the poet himself.

glosses.zh: 重衾：一层层的被子。衾，被子。
glosses.en: chóng qīn: layers of quilts. Qīn means a quilt.

glosses.zh: 载将：装载着。将，助词，没有实在的意思。
glosses.en: zài jiāng: carrying. Jiāng here is a little helper word with no meaning of its own.

glosses.zh: 旧客京华：从前客居在京城。京华，京城，指开封。
glosses.en: jiù kè jīng huá: staying as a guest in the capital in the past. Jīng huá means the capital, Kaifeng.

glosses.zh: 偎傍：亲热地靠在一起。
glosses.en: wēi bàng: sitting close together, leaning on each other.

glosses.zh: 小槛：小栏杆，指有栏杆的小亭子、小楼。
glosses.en: xiǎo jiàn: a small railing, meaning a little pavilion or tower with railings.

glosses.zh: 冶叶倡条：美丽的柳叶柳条，比喻歌女。冶，美丽。
glosses.en: yě yè chāng tiáo: pretty willow leaves and branches, a picture for the singing girls of the city. Yě means pretty.

glosses.zh: 珠歌翠舞：歌声圆润像珠子，舞女穿戴着翠绿的饰品跳舞。
glosses.en: zhū gē cuì wǔ: songs as smooth as pearls, and dancers in green jewels.

glosses.zh: 水驿：水路上的驿站，给来往的人歇脚的地方。
glosses.en: shuǐ yì: a stopping place on a water route, where travellers rest.

glosses.zh: 夜如岁：一夜长得像一年。
glosses.en: yè rú suì: one night feels as long as a year.

glosses.zh: 无憀：无聊，心里空落落的，没有依靠。
glosses.en: wú liáo: lonely and empty, with nothing to lean on.

glosses.zh: 凝想：出神地想。
glosses.en: níng xiǎng: thinking hard, lost in thought.

glosses.zh: 鸳侣：像鸳鸯一样的伴侣，指心爱的人。鸳鸯是总成双成对的水鸟。
glosses.en: yuān lǚ: a partner like a mandarin duck, meaning one's beloved. Mandarin ducks are water birds that always go in pairs.

translation.en: The road along the Sui Dyke.

translation.zh: 天渐渐晚了，深深的树林里升起浓雾。
translation.en: As the day grows late, thick mist rises from the deep woods.

translation.zh: 昏暗的夜里，淡淡的月光笼罩着沙岸，
translation.en: In the dim night, pale moonlight wraps the sandy bank,

translation.zh: 我又要住在河桥边僻静的地方。
translation.en: and once more I must stay by the river bridge, far from anyone.

translation.zh: 一点也不管烟波已经把我和送别的地方隔开，
translation.en: does not care at all that the misty water now cuts me off from the place of parting.

translation.zh: 只等我这个远行的人醉着裹上厚厚的被子，
translation.en: It only waits for me, the traveller, to curl up drunk in my quilts,

translation.zh: 就载着满船离愁开走了。
translation.en: and then carries me off with a boatload of parting sorrow.

translation.zh: 于是我想起从前住在京城的日子，
translation.en: So I think of the days when I stayed in the capital,

translation.zh: 常常和朋友们在稀疏的树林边、小楼栏杆旁亲热地相聚。
translation.en: when we often gathered close together by thin woods and little railed towers.

translation.zh: 那些美丽的歌女我个个都认识，
translation.en: I knew every one of the pretty singing girls,

translation.zh: 早就看惯了她们圆润的歌声和翩翩的舞姿。
translation.en: and I was used to their pearl-smooth songs and dances in green jewels.

translation.zh: 如今我却到了渔村和水边的驿站，
translation.en: Now I have come to fishing villages and river inns,

translation.zh: 一夜长得像一年，只能烧着香，自己跟自己说话。
translation.en: where one night lasts a year, and I burn incense and talk to myself.

translation.zh: 有谁会想到我这样孤单无聊呢？
translation.en: Who would think of me, so lonely and lost?

translation.zh: 只有梦里，我还在出神地想着心爱的人。
translation.en: Only in my dreams do I still think, lost in thought, of my beloved.

background.zh: 这首词写诗人离开京城开封，坐船沿着汴河远行。傍晚船走在隋堤边，雾起月出，他想起在京城时和朋友、歌女一起欢聚的日子，对比如今一个人住在渔村驿站的冷清。周邦彦一生几次离开京城到外地做官，这首词具体写在哪一次，现在说不清楚。
background.en: In this lyric the poet leaves the capital, Kaifeng, and travels by boat down the Bian River. At dusk the boat passes the Sui Dyke, mist rises and the moon comes out. He remembers happy times in the capital with friends and singing girls, and compares them with the loneliness of staying at fishing villages and river inns. Zhou Bangyan left the capital several times to serve in other places, and we cannot say which journey this was.

author_note.zh: 周邦彦（1056—1121），字美成，号清真居士，钱塘（今浙江杭州）人。他精通音乐，晚年曾管理朝廷的音乐机构大晟府。他的词很会写景，常常把景物和心情一层一层地铺开，这首词就是先写眼前，再写回忆，最后回到眼前。
author_note.en: Zhou Bangyan (1056–1121), also called Meicheng, came from Qiantang, today's Hangzhou. He knew music deeply and in later life ran the court's music office. He was very good at painting scenes in words and often laid out scenery and feeling layer by layer. This lyric moves from the present to a memory and back to the present.

appreciation.zh: 开头三个字“隋堤路”，就把人放到了长长的柳堤上。天黑了，树林里起雾，月光淡淡的，他又要在河桥边过夜。最有意思的是他怪那只船“无情”：它才不管我和亲人被烟波隔开，只等我喝醉了裹上被子，就载着满船离愁开走。其实无情的不是船，是离别。下阕他想起京城的热闹：朋友相聚，歌女的歌舞，样样都熟悉。再看现在，渔村、驿站，一夜长得像一年，只能烧香自言自语。最后一句说，没人想着我，我只能在梦里想你。热闹和冷清一比，孤单就更深了。
appreciation.en: The opening words, "the road along the Sui Dyke", put us right on the long willow bank. Night falls, mist rises from the woods, the moonlight is pale, and once again he must spend the night by the river bridge. The most interesting part is that he blames the boat for being heartless. It does not care that the misty water cuts him off from the ones he loves; it just waits until he is drunk and wrapped in his quilts, then sails off with a boatload of sorrow. Of course the heartless thing is not the boat but the parting. The second stanza recalls the lively capital: friends together, the songs and dances, all so familiar. Then back to now: fishing villages, river inns, a night that lasts a year, burning incense and talking to himself. At the end he says no one thinks of him, and he can only think of his beloved in dreams. Set beside the lively past, the loneliness feels deeper.
